rows.exact_result: HISTORICAL_CAPACITY_CONFOUNDED: original A->B ~1.879 bpm (~20.6% relative, sometimes miscited as ~23%) used Model A (8,065 params) vs Model B (28,865/29,089 params) - NOT capacity-matched. Capacity control (docs/PPG_DALIA_CAPACITY_CONTROL_PREDECLARATION.md) found ~68% of this gap is recovered by capacity/architecture alone (A_cap). The GOVERNING capacity-controlled result is: A_cap->B ~0.605 bpm, C->B ~0.776 bpm, both 5/5 seeds (results/ppg_dalia_capacity_control.json). Per docs/FURKAN_PAPER_HANDOFF_CANONICAL_DAY9.md: do NOT write 20.6%/23% pure IMU, 1.88 bpm clean IMU, or a 59/41 causal split.

rows.exact_result: STAGE 3 UPDATE (full CV complete): A real BLOCKER was found (6/24 subjects had corrupted reference ECG, near-zero detectable R-peaks) via hostile review of a full 6-fold CV. Fixed (real R-peak-rate eligibility gate added), corrected eligibility=18/24. Full corrected 6-fold CV completed (5 newly-trained folds + 1 independently re-verified reused fold): participant-level A_cap->B=+0.834 bpm (12/18 favor B), C->B=+0.916 bpm (13/18 favor B); window-weighted (33,813 pooled test windows) A_cap->B=+0.845 bpm, C->B=+0.920 bpm. No sign reversal under either aggregation or leave-one-out exclusion of the most extreme subject. Both the pre-fix single-fold diagnostic and the pre-fix full 6-fold CV remain marked INVALIDATED_BY_REFERENCE_SIGNAL_QUALITY_DEFECT. See results/galaxyppg_corrected_full_cv_result.json and docs/GALAXYPPG_STAGE3_CORRECTED_RESULTS.md.
rows.n_subjects: 24 total, 18 real reference-ECG-quality-eligible (6 excluded for a real corrupted-reference-ECG data-integrity defect)
rows.sensitivity: Real subject heterogeneity disclosed: 6/18 subjects favor A_cap over B, 5/18 favor C over B. No sign reversal at the aggregate level under window-weighted vs participant-level aggregation or under leave-one-out exclusion of the single most extreme subject (P16).
rows.replication_state: EXTERNAL_REPLICATION_SUPPORTIVE (full corrected 6-fold CV, n=18 biological participants)
rows.burden_relevance: same as PPG-DaLiA row - wrist IMU near-zero marginal burden
rows.limitations: Real, moderate, heterogeneous effect - not uniform across subjects (see sensitivity). Smaller in magnitude than the earlier bounded single-fold diagnostic (+1.342/+1.629 bpm on 3/3 subjects), which the full cohort reveals was not representative of the whole 18-subject population.
rows.safe_claim: Aligned wrist IMU added a real but moderate and heterogeneous HR-estimation benefit under a capacity-near-matched comparison on GalaxyPPG (full corrected 6-fold CV, n=18 biological participants, A_cap->B +0.834 bpm, C->B +0.916 bpm, majority of subjects favor B, no aggregate sign reversal) - qualitatively consistent with PPG-DaLiA's capacity-controlled finding, though smaller and less uniform than the earlier bounded single-fold diagnostic suggested.

rows.exact_result: STAGE 3 UPDATE (protocol-compliant rerun, HIGH-03 remediation): REAL TRAINING COMPLETE under the frozen 0-60mmHg scope. Real eligibility: 12/16 subjects have valid pleth (4 excluded, real data-quality finding). 200/607 windows excluded for being outside the frozen 0-60mmHg scope (407 in-scope windows used). LOSO (n=12): A=20.973, B=21.425, C=20.132 (MAE mmHg). A-B=-0.452 (3/12 favor B, SIGN-REVERSES if subject 9 excluded). C-B=-1.293 (5/12 favor B over C; B worse than its own different-stage-enforced deranged control, but shrinks substantially without subject 9). COMPLETE_MIXED (substantial subject heterogeneity, not a uniform negative). Real per-subject heterogeneity: subjects 4 and 9 are extreme opposite-direction outliers on A-B. The prior 607-window execution (A=27.62, B=29.86, C=29.83, A-B=-2.24, subjects 4/7 framing, COMPLETE_NEGATIVE) included 200 out-of-scope windows and a C-control with same-stage leakage - HISTORICAL_SUPERSEDED_OUT_OF_PROTOCOL, never cite its numbers as current. See results/lbnp_thoracic_eis_stage3_v2_protocol_compliant.json and docs/LBNP_STAGE3_HIGH03_REMEDIATION.md.
rows.sensitivity: A-B sign-reverses under leave-one-out exclusion of subject 9 (an extreme outlier); C-B remains negative under leave-one-out but shrinks substantially without subject 9 - both key comparisons are partly driven by one influential subject, not a stable cohort-wide effect. Subjects 4 and 9 are the extreme opposite-direction outliers on A-B (not subjects 4/7, which was the prior out-of-protocol run's framing under a different, larger window set).
rows.burden_relevance: thoracic EIS electrodes are a real, distinct contact-region/module burden from ECG/pleth
rows.limitations: n=12 (not 16) due to real pleth-quality exclusion; only thoracic site tested; both A-B and C-B comparisons are subject-9-sensitive
rows.safe_claim: Corrected LBNP shows no stable aggregate incremental thoracic EIS benefit over ECG+pleth under the frozen terrestrial 0-60 mmHg protocol, with substantial subject heterogeneity - a real but heterogeneous (COMPLETE_MIXED), not uniformly negative, result.
